title: Keel: Declarative priv-EKS provisioner Terraform module + canary upgrade playbook
creator: Marina Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (Keel) that provisions and manages Redwood Private control-plane EKS clusters with an opinionated, declarative API. Keel will: create control-plane resources (EKS control plane, IAM roles, KMS-backed secrets), bootstrap nodepool blueprints for managed nodegroups, expose lifecycle hooks for safe canary upgrades, and emit health signals to Console. The module must be composable (seed vs fleet), idempotent, and friendly for air-gapped / VPC-restricted installs.
acceptance_criteria: Keel Terraform module publishes as a registry module and can be consumed in a sample customer VPC to create a control plane end-to-end
Successful canary upgrade: control plane patch rolled to 5% of clusters, automated health gates prevented rollout on simulated kube-apiserver errors
Module supports KMS-integrated secret creation and rotates via documented steps
Module exposes Prometheus metrics and structured logs that Console ingestion parses (controlplane_health, upgrade_progress, reconcile_duration_ms)
Idempotent runs: repeated apply on unchanged config results in no drift and no destructive changes
design_notes: Decision: use EKS managed control plane (eksctl/eks api) with opinionated add-ons rather than fully self-managed k8s master to reduce operator complexity
Trade-off: managed control plane obscures some upgrade internals; mitigated by adding probe-level health gates and richer telemetry
Hook model: module exposes 'pre_patch', 'post_patch', 'pre_delete' lifecycle hooks allowing ops scripts (SQS/SNS or Lambda) to run validations
Naming: resource names use project-prefix + cluster-id to avoid cross-tenant collisions; encryption keys are per-account with optional cross-account grants
upgrade_strategy: Two-phase canary: 1) control-plane nodegroup patch on a single cluster (10% traffic equivalent), run test suite; 2) staggered rollout with exponential backoff and automatic rollback on health gate failure
Fallback: automatic routing of new customer requests to compatible model-serving tier when controlplane is degraded
Safety gates: prometheus rules + lambda health-checker + manual approval window configurable via module variable 'upgrade_security_level'
health_checks: kube-apiserver reachable and <100ms p95 latency under synthetic load
etcd leader stable and <5% measurement errors across 5m window
TLS cert expiration > 7 days warning alert and auto-rotation playbook link provided
observability_integration: Emit structured events to Console ingestion endpoint (/events/controlplane) with keys: cluster_id, event_type, severity, trace_id
Expose Prometheus scrape endpoints for controlplane components; default scrape interval 30s
Tracing: add X-Trace header propagation hooks into bootstrapper for cross-service traces
test_plan: Unit tests for Terraform module using terratest and kitchen-terraform
End-to-end integration test in sandbox VPC: full create -> simulated traffic -> upgrade -> rollback
Chaos job: terminate controlplane worker instance during upgrade to validate automatic rollback
Security: run static TF scans (tfsec), IAM diff analysis, and KMS key policy review
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal staging account (one cluster) — smoke tests and metrics baseline
Stage 1: alpha customers (non-critical) with feature flag controlled via Console
Stage 2: broader fleet with rolling canary and telemetry monitoring
Stage 3: GA — enable by default for new Private customers and document migration path for existing clusters
migration_notes: Provide a migration helper script to import existing EKS control planes into Keel's state using 'terraform import' and a validation run
Legacy clusters will be put into 'compatibility mode' where Keel only manages upgrades when explicit consent is provided
Data plane impact minimized by ensuring nodegroup replacement uses scale-up before scale-down pattern
implementation_todos: Finish Terraform module core resources: eks cluster, IAM roles, kms_key, security_groups
Add lifecycle hook resources and sample Lambda validation script
Wire up Prometheus exporter for controlplane metrics and test Console ingestion
Draft runbook for manual rollback and emergency upgrade paths
blockers: Pending KMS cross-account grant policy decision from Security (sec-req-221)
Need transient sandbox capacity quota increase from Cloud Infra to run integration canaries
notes: Aim to keep module variables minimal and provide sensible defaults; prefer explicit opt-in for destructive features
Coordinate with Console team to add new dashboard widgets for Keel-provisioned clusters
Document resource tagging and billing attributes to map clusters back to customer tenants
